title: Exactness of the Cech sequence of a module is equivalent to bijectivity of the comparison map on f-power torsion
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes the exactness of the Cech sequence of an arbitrary module for a ring map inducing isomorphisms modulo all powers of a fixed element: exactness on the right always holds, exactness on the left is equivalent to injectivity of the comparison map on power torsion, and exactness in the middle is equivalent to its surjectivity, with the resulting characterization of glueability and its specialization to glueing pairs and to the completion (statement lines 25364-25385). The proof of the middle case is an explicit element computation in which one first reduces to the torsion-free case, then treats the universal example of the ring modulo its power torsion submodule, where the Tor group vanishes by an earlier computation, and finally passes to a general module through a free presentation whose sequence remains exact after tensoring because of the completion statement (proof lines 25387-25423). The reduction to the universal case and the presentation step are the substantive moves. The counted span refers three times, twice to results of this chapter and once to a result of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
